CAMDEN, N.J. and BRYN MAWR, Pa. , Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- American Water Works Company, Inc. (NYSE: AWK) ("American Water") and Essential Utilities, Inc. (NYSE: WTRG) ("Essential Utilities") today announced that the Illinois Commerce Commission issued an order approving the companies' proposed merger, marking the fourth favorable regulatory action toward completion of the transaction.

The companies previously received approval of the merger from the following regulatory commissions:

  • Virginia State Corporation Commission on June 22, 2026;
  • Public Utilities Commission of Ohio on May 13, 2026; and
  • Kentucky Public Service Commission on April 21, 2026.

Providing further momentum, settlement agreements in the merger approval proceedings have been reached in Pennsylvania, North Carolina, Texas, and New Jersey. Each agreement remains subject to review and approval by the applicable public utility commission.

Additionally, the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act expired on August 14, 2026, and shareholders of both companies overwhelmingly approved the transaction earlier this year.

The all-stock merger, announced October 27, 2025, will create a combined company serving more than 4.7 million water and wastewater customer connections and more than 740,000 natural gas customer connections. The combined company will operate under the American Water name and be headquartered in Camden, New Jersey.

The merger is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2027, but remains subject to customary closing conditions, including, among others, required regulatory approvals, including approval from the remaining applicable public utility commissions.

For additional details regarding the transaction, please visit americanwateressentialutilitiesmerger.com.

About American Water
American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. American Water's approximately 7,000 talented professionals leverage their significant expertise and the company's national size and scale to achieve excellent outcomes for the benefit of customers, employees, investors and other stakeholders. For more information, visit amwater.com and join American Water on LinkedIn, Facebook, X and Instagram.

About Essential Utilities
Essential Utilities, Inc. (NYSE: WTRG) delivers safe, clean, reliable services that improve quality of life for individuals, families, and entire communities. With a focus on water, wastewater, and natural gas, Essential is committed to sustainable growth, operational excellence, a superior customer experience, and premier employer status. We are advocates for the communities we serve and are dedicated stewards of natural lands, protecting thousands of acres of forests and other habitats throughout our footprint.  Operating as the Aqua and Peoples brands, Essential serves approximately 5.5 million people across nine states. Essential is one of the most significant publicly traded water, wastewater service and natural gas providers in the U.S. Learn more at www.essential.co.

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kestrel Group Ltd (NASDAQ: KG) ("Kestrel" or the "Company") a leading specialty insurance platform that provides fronting services to program managers, reinsurers, and reinsurance brokers, today reported its financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Key Highlights – Third Quarter 2026 Financials

  • Program Services fee income of $2.9 million, up 203% year over year with a 71% margin on fee revenue
  • Program Services fee revenue of $4.1 million, up 151% year over year
  • Premium produced(1) by Program Services clients was $121.2 million, up 132% year over year
  • Total revenues were $4.8 million
  • Net premiums earned were $1.9 million
  • As of September 30, 2026, the Company's book value per common share(2) was $12.44
  • Net loss was $16.4 million, or a loss of $2.09 per share

Commenting on the results, Kestrel's Chief Executive Officer, Luke Ledbetter, stated, "Our Program Services segment continues to demonstrate strong sequential growth, with fee income, fee revenue and premium produced up once again, both from the second quarter of 2026 and year-over-year. This marks improvement in each quarter of 2026, driven by solid execution and our expanding pipeline of opportunity, and we are encouraged by the positive momentum within this segment. As we focus on the areas of our business with the greatest potential return for shareholders, we remain committed to optimizing our cost structure. Toward that end, we are pursuing broad-based expense reduction initiatives which have made significant progress during the third quarter, and we are targeting approximately $5 million in run-rate expense savings over the next year."

Program Services Segment

The Program Services segment provides fronting services to general agents and insurance carriers to leverage Kestrel's trusted reputation to provide access to the U.S. property and casualty insurance market and insurance paper rated "A-" (Excellent) by A.M. Best and expansive licenses in exchange for fees. Kestrel issues the policy through exclusive use of four insurance carriers, and those carriers presently retain and reinsure the risk. The Company continues to actively pursue reinsurance mechanisms with its existing partners that would selectively deploy the Company's underwriting capacity that it believes could facilitate and accelerate both its fee and premium revenue growth.

Program Services' fee income for the third quarter of 2026 was $2.9 million, up 203% compared to the same quarter in 2025. Total fee revenues for the quarter were $4.1 million, up 151% from the third quarter of 2025, driven by growth in both existing and new client accounts. Premium produced(1) by client programs totaled $121.2 million for the quarter, up 132% year over year.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Program Services' fee income was $6.9 million, compared to $1.0 million for the same period in 2025. Total fee revenues for the period were $10.9 million, compared to $3.0 million in 2025, reflecting higher premium produced by both new and existing client programs. Premium produced(1) for the nine months totaled $325.0 million, up 244% from the prior-year period.

Legacy Reinsurance Segment

The Legacy Reinsurance segment consists of the AmTrust Reinsurance and Diversified Reinsurance segments previously reported by Maiden Holdings, Ltd. ("Maiden") prior to the Combination with Kestrel. The AmTrust portion of this segment includes all business ceded to Maiden Reinsurance Ltd. by AmTrust. The Diversified portion of this segment consists of a run-off portfolio of predominantly third-party property and casualty reinsurance business focusing on regional and specialty property and casualty insurance companies located primarily in Europe, as well as business produced by Maiden LF and Maiden GF along with transactions entered into by Genesis Legacy Solutions.

During the third quarter of 2026, the Legacy Reinsurance segment reported an underwriting loss of $6.4 million, consisting of $0.1 million of underwriting income from the AmTrust business and a $6.5 million underwriting loss from the Diversified business.

The AmTrust business reported a current accident year underwriting loss of $1.4 million as the run-off of certain remaining multiple-year policies continues. This was offset by net favorable prior period development ("PPD") of $1.4 million, primarily experienced from movement not subject to the LPT/ADC Agreement including favorable movement in Workers' Compensation and Program exposure partially offset by adverse development in Specialty Risk lines of business in the AmTrust Quota Share. PPD was also affected by foreign currency movements on loss reserves denominated in non-USD currencies, which had an adverse impact of $1.3 million. Excluding foreign exchange, PPD for the AmTrust business was favorable by $2.7 million.

The Diversified business' results largely reflect the ongoing run-off of the Company's international operations. Its $6.5 million underwriting loss included $3.1 million of loss development on the German Auto quota share in the IIS unit, after the cedant triggered contractual inflation-related adjustments that increased the Company's exposure, and a $2.4 million settlement of a Genesis Legacy Solutions claim.

Investment Activities and Other Gains

The Company reported a net loss from investment activities of $1.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, consisting of net investment income of $2.3 million, offset by net realized and unrealized investment losses of $3.6 million, which reflected fair value adjustments on certain of the Company's alternative and real estate assets.

The Company also recognized foreign exchange and other gains of $0.7 million for the quarter, primarily consisting of $0.5 million of net foreign exchange gains and a $0.1 million gain from the revaluation of a contingent receivable in the insurance distribution industry. The foreign exchange gains resulted from the appreciation of the U.S. dollar on the remeasurement of net loss reserves and insurance-related liabilities denominated in non-USD currencies.

General and Administrative Expenses

Total general and administrative expenses were $11.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $11.8 million for the third quarter of 2025. Segment G&A expenses fell to $3.4 million from $4.4 million. Corporate G&A expenses rose to $8.0 million from $7.4 million. The increase was driven mainly by higher share-based compensation of $1.6 million (versus $0.2 million) and by higher recurring compensation, legal and professional fees. Lower non-recurring expenses of $0.5 million (versus $2.3 million) partly offset these increases.

Segment G&A expenses for the quarter included $0.3 million in fair value adjustments recognized in connection with the Company's May 27, 2025 combination with Maiden. Non-recurring segment G&A expense includes costs for the GLS arbitration while non-recurring corporate G&A expenses include costs for the restructuring and severance (including $0.5 million of employee separation charges incurred in the quarter) and the Combination. These costs are excluded from the Company's non-GAAP operating loss. See "Non-GAAP Financial Measures."

The Company is carrying out broad-based initiatives to reduce its operating cost structure. It expects these actions to produce annualized run-rate savings of approximately $5 million, with the full run-rate expected within the next twelve months. Actions taken to date include:

  • significantly reducing costs associated with a broad range of professional and advisory services;
  • outsourcing a substantial portion of the Company's information technology infrastructure and support functions, completed early in the fourth quarter of 2026; and
  • streamlining certain internal functions, including related headcount reductions and the selective use of third-party service providers.

The Company continues to evaluate and implement a range of additional measures and may incur additional employee separation and other non-recurring charges as these initiatives are completed.

Balance Sheet

Total assets were $879.6 million at September 30, 2026, and shareholders' equity was $97.8 million.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company has available net operating loss ("NOL") carryforwards of $477.8 million for income tax purposes. Approximately $390.2 million of NOL carryforwards expire in various years beginning in 2029. As of September 30, 2026, approximately $87.6 million or 18.3% of the Company's NOL carryforwards have no expiry date under the relevant U.S. tax law.

Investor Presentation

The Company has posted an investor presentation on its website in connection with this earnings release. The presentation, dated November 2026, can be found at https://kestrelgroup.gcs-web.com/events-and-presentations/presentations.

Book value per common share is calculated using shareholders' equity divided by the number of common shares outstanding excluding unvested restricted and performance shares. Management uses growth in this metric as a prime measure of the value we are generating for our common shareholders, because management believes that growth in this metric ultimately results in growth in the Company's common share price. It also excludes on a non-recurring basis: (1) litigation costs related to the GLS Arbitration; (2) restructuring and severance costs; and (3) costs incurred due to the Combination; (4) Change in fair value of earn out consideration; and (5) Change in bargain purchase gain. Non-GAAP operating earnings should not be viewed as a substitute for U.S. GAAP net income.



(6)

Kyoto event generates approximately US$1.3 million in service revenue for FiEE, highlighting opportunities in next-generation art discovery and collector engagement

OSAKA, Japan, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FiEE, Inc. (NASDAQ: FIEE) ("FiEE" or the "Company"), a technology company integrating Internet of Things ("IoT"), connectivity, and artificial intelligence ("AI") to redefine brand management solutions, today announced the successful completion of its international art exhibition and accompanying auction in Kyoto, Japan. The event marks a milestone in FiEE's evolution toward an online-to-offline ("O2O") ecosystem integrating art and technology ("ArtTech"), connecting artists and global collectors through digital engagement, physical experiences, and commercial transactions.

Organized by the Company's subsidiary, FiEE Channel Limited, in partnership with the Museum of Kyoto, Harmony of Ink: FAx26 Kyoto International Contemporary Art Exchange Exhibition took place from October 23 to 25, 2026. The accompanying auction, held on October 23, 2026, attracted nearly 400 participants online and in person, resulting in an aggregate artwork transaction value of approximately US$2.9 million. The aggregate transaction value represents artwork sales, not the Company's revenue. FiEE generated approximately US$1.3 million in service revenue from the auction, highlighting the commercial potential of its O2O business model. Building on this success, FiEE plans to organize regular art appreciation and networking events to deepen collector engagement and create additional revenue opportunities.

Discovering hidden gems: Engaging the next generation of collectors

FiEE sees opportunities to engage younger collectors, including millennials (Generation Y) and members of Generation Z, who seek originality, cultural identity, and emerging artistic talent beyond established names.

Leveraging its network of key opinion leaders ("KOLs"), digital content capabilities, and curated exhibitions, FiEE aims to connect artists with collectors seeking distinctive artworks and hidden gems. By combining online discovery with physical experiences, the Company seeks to make art more accessible while expanding international exposure for artists.

Beyond transactions: Art advisory as a service

FiEE believes artwork acquisition should mark the beginning of a lasting collector relationship. The Company sees opportunities to develop art advisory services that would offer personalized artwork recommendations, artist introductions, acquisition assistance, collection development, and post-transaction support.

Complementary offerings, including artwork safekeeping, promotional services, and exhibition opportunities, could further strengthen collector relationships. By extending engagement beyond individual purchases, FiEE aims to encourage repeat transactions and generate advisory fees and recurring service revenue, supporting a more diversified business model.

Connecting online discovery with offline experiences

FiEE's O2O strategy integrates digital engagement with physical cultural experiences, creating a connected journey from artwork discovery to acquisition. The Company's software-as-a-service ("SaaS") solutions support this strategy. The FiEE Channel App supports content creation, social media amplification, and audience acquisition, while the Fontree App enables online participation in curated art sales and facilitates transactions. Physical exhibitions and private events are intended to complement these platforms, allowing collectors to experience artworks firsthand and build relationships with artists.

Together, these channels create opportunities for continued engagement, repeat participation, and additional value-added services.

Rafael Li, Chief Executive Officer and President of FiEE, commented, "The success of our Kyoto art exhibition and accompanying auction highlights FiEE's ability to translate digital engagement into meaningful commercial transactions while establishing a foundation for a broader ArtTech ecosystem. We see exciting opportunities among younger collectors seeking hidden gems and emerging talent. By seeking to combine personalized art advisory, curated experiences, and a global collector network, we aim to make art discovery more accessible and rewarding.

"Our vision extends beyond individual transactions. We aim to connect online discovery with offline experiences and build lasting relationships between artists and collectors, with the goal of unlocking new revenue opportunities and creating long-term value for our stockholders."

About FiEE, Inc.

FiEE, Inc. (NASDAQ: FIEE), formerly Minim, Inc., was founded in 1977. It has a historical track record of delivering a comprehensive WiFi/SaaS platform in the market. After years of development, it made the strategic decision to transition to a Software First Model in 2024 to expand its technology portfolio and revenue streams. In 2025, FiEE, Inc. rebranded itself as a technology company leveraging its expertise in IoT, connectivity, and AI to explore new business prospects and extend its global footprint.

FiEE, Inc.'s services are structured into four key categories: Cloud-Managed Connectivity (WiFi) Platform, IoT Hardware Sales & Licensing, SaaS Solutions, and Professional To-C and To-B Services & Support. Notably, FiEE, Inc. has introduced its innovative SaaS solutions, which integrate its AI and data analytics capabilities into content creation and brand management. This initiative has nurtured a robust pool of KOLs on major social media platforms worldwide, helping them develop, manage, and optimize their digital presence. FiEE, Inc.'s services include customized graphics and posts, short videos, and editorial calendars tailored to align with brand objectives.

About the Ntrust℠ Clinical Trials in Autoimmune Disease
Ntrust-1 (NCT06557265) and Ntrust-2 (NCT06733935) are multi-center, open-label, dose-escalation clinical trials in patients with autoimmune disease receiving lymphodepletion followed by CD19-targeted CAR-NK cell therapy. Both trials assess the safety of NKX019 in people living with autoimmune diseases as well as its potential to achieve durable remission via a “reset” of the immune system through the elimination of pathogenic B cells.  

The Ntrust trials are enrolling up to 12 patients per dose level per disease indication, with leading indications in myositis and systemic sclerosis, as well as ANCA-associated vasculitis, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus nephritis, and primary membranous nephropathy. Additional patients may be enrolled if needed to refine patient populations for further study.

In both studies, patients receive a three-dose cycle of NKX019 following lymphodepletion with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide or cyclophosphamide alone, if they have significant cytopenia at baseline. This approach is designed to evaluate the single-agent activity of NKX019 and facilitate a more rapid path to regulatory approval. Patients in both trials may also receive additional cycles, if needed, to restore response or enable a deeper response.
   
About NKX019
NKX019 is an allogeneic, cryopreserved, off-the-shelf immunotherapy candidate that uses natural killer (NK) cells derived from the peripheral blood of healthy adult donors. It is engineered with a humanized CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) for enhanced cell targeting and a proprietary, membrane-bound form of interleukin-15 (IL-15) for greater persistence and activity without exogenous cytokine support. CD19 is a biomarker for normal B cells as well as those implicated in autoimmune disease. Nkarta is evaluating NKX019 in multiple autoimmune conditions.

Nkarta is a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing the development of allogeneic, off-the-shelf natural killer (NK) cell therapies for people living with autoimmune diseases. By harnessing the power of the innate immune system to eliminate pathogenic B cells driving the autoimmune response, Nkarta is advancing novel cell therapies engineered for deep therapeutic impact. Real-world study data can provide valuable insights into how treatments work outside of controlled clinical trial settings. Real-world data analyses also have several limitations; while associations can be demonstrated, causal relationships cannot be definitively established. Results may reflect potential unmeasured confounding, the relatively recent approval of both treatments limited follow-up duration, and electronic medical record data may be subject to coding inaccuracies.

About PLATINUM-Truveta
PLATINUM-Truveta was an observational, retrospective cohort study that used de-identified electronic medical record data from the Truveta database across 30 US health systems from June 2021 through March 2026. Adults with MASH who initiated semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly injection (n=2,873) or resmetirom (n=2,285) were included. Changes from baseline in ALT, AST, body weight, HbA1c, platelets, triglycerides, HDL, and LDL were assessed at three and six months. Patients with prior use of semaglutide or resmetirom, cirrhosis or other chronic liver diseases were excluded, and treatment persistence was required at each time point. To reduce confounding, generalized estimating equations with inverse probability of treatment weighting were applied. Patients in the semaglutide group were defined as having MASH if they had one or more claims with a diagnosis code for MASH (ICD-10 CM K75.81) in the 12 month period before index date.1

About RHODIUM-2
RHODIUM-2 was an observational, retrospective study that used de-identified electronic medical record data from the Truveta database across more than 30 US health systems from June 2021 through March 2026. Adults with MASH were grouped according to whether they initiated semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly injection (n=2,479) or did not initiate semaglutide (n=70,702). Changes from baseline in ALT, AST, body weight, and HbA1c were assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months. Patients with cirrhosis or other liver disease etiologies and those treated with GLP-1 receptor agonists or resmetirom within six months before start of first treatment were excluded. To control for confounding, generalized estimating equations to account for within patient correlation, and inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied.2

About metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH)
MASH is a serious, progressive, metabolic disease affecting the liver, which can be fatal if not managed properly.3 More than 250 million people live with MASH,4 and the number of individuals in advanced stages of the disease is expected to increase over 160% from 2015 to 2030.5 Of those living with overweight or obesity, more than one in three also have MASH.6 And of those currently living with MASH, more than 40% have type 2 diabetes, and more than 8 in 10 also live with obesity.7 People living with MASH often have many other health-related comorbidities,8 such as cardiovascular disease, which is the leading cause of death in people with MASH.9,10

MASH is largely a silent disease due to few and unspecific symptoms in its early stages,3 where nearly 90% of people with MASH remain undiagnosed.11 Once MASH progresses to late stages, there is increased mortality and morbidity, including potential for cirrhosis, liver cancer, and need for liver transplant.12

About semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly injection in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH)
Semaglutide 2.4 mg is a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) FDA-approved under accelerated approval to treat adults with MASH with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring (fibrosis), but not with cirrhosis of the liver, in conjunction with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity.13 This accelerated approval is based on improvement of MASH and liver scarring (fibrosis).13 Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon the verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial.13 Novo is investigating semaglutide 2.4 mg in the ongoing ESSENCE phase 3 trial, evaluating the effect of once weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg in adults with MASH with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring (fibrosis) (consistent with stage F2 or F3†).13

It is important to note that semaglutide 2.4 mg injection has a Boxed Warning for possible thyroid tumors, including cancer, and should not be used in those with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN 2). The most common side effects of semaglutide include: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, stomach (abdomen) pain, changes in skin sensations, headache, tiredness (fatigue), upset stomach, dizziness, feeling bloated, belching, low blood sugar in people with type 2 diabetes, gas, stomach flu, heartburn, and hair loss.13
